findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the intended behavior for an archived or deleted Jira version (keep on ticket / remove / alert) as a settled decision, not just a topic the ADR must cover.
evidence: Step 1 ADR 'must cover ... what happens when a Jira version is archived or deleted.'
The 'Design decisions (all settled 2026-11-05)' list covers Cardinality, Direction, Entity, Affects versions, Hierarchy — but NOT archived/deleted handling.
AC: 'records ... archived/deleted version handling' states it must be recorded but not what the behavior is.
findings.finding: The archived/deleted Jira version behavior is a real design decision the plan requires the ADR to make but provides no decision or default direction, unlike the other design choices which are marked DECIDED.
findings.location: Approach step 1 / Design decisions section / AC line 1
scenarios: A Jira version bound to a rebar ticket is archived or deleted; the executor has no stated direction for whether the release stays, is removed, or raises an alert.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a 'Archived/deleted version: DECIDED ...' bullet to the Design decisions section mirroring the Missing-version decision (e.g. keep the release on the rebar ticket, raise a BRIDGE_ALERT, do not auto-remove).

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the rollout/rollback story for the new outbound fixVersions write: how it reaches production safely (e.g. inbound-only first pass, a dormant/observe mode, or a documented kill path) and how an operator cheaply halts or reverses release writes to Jira without data cleanup, given the 'no config key' constraint.
evidence: 'A bridged project needs no new setting. The field syncs whenever the bridge runs.'
Final AC validates on 'the production bridge, after deploy' with no mention of a flag/canary or a way to disable the outbound fixVersions write
The outbound arm mutates external Jira state (fixVersions add/remove verbs), so a bad write is not a pure-local revert
findings.finding: The plan changes runtime behavior of a deployed, long-running bridge that now writes to Jira (fixVersions) in both directions, but specifies no staged rollout, flag, canary, or rollback path; the 'No config key' constraint forces the new write to activate for every bridged project on deploy.
findings.location: Constraints ('No config key'); final non-codebase Acceptance Criterion
scenarios: First deploy mis-maps a release name and the bridge begins adding/removing fixVersions on many REB issues across all bridged projects at once
Operator needs to stop outbound release writes quickly while keeping the rest of the bridge running
findings.suggested_fix: Add a Rollout/rollback subsection: e.g. ship inbound-read + local field first, gate the outbound Jira write behind a reversible marker (tied to the epic's sunset-ticket mechanism already allowed by the constraints), and document that disabling the bridge or the marker stops further writes while existing per-item add/remove verbs leave prior Jira state recoverable.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Have the ADR specify how missing-version retry coexists with 'No churn': e.g. emit the BRIDGE_ALERT once, suppress it while already open for the same ticket+version, retry the outbound write without writing a new event on an unchanged pass, and emit a resolving BRIDGE_ALERT only when the version appears.
evidence: Plan: 'the bridge does not write it; ... a BRIDGE_ALERT names the missing version, and each pass retries until the version exists'
Plan constraint: 'A first pass over an unchanged store writes only initial values; a repeat pass writes nothing.'

dispatch_one.create_one writes a fresh BRIDGE_ALERT event file each time (ts+uuid-named); process_bridge_alert supports resolve-by-uuid, so an open-and-resolve model is available but the plan does not say the alert is emitted once and suppressed while open.
findings.finding: The missing-version retry mechanism and the 'No churn' constraint are in tension and the plan does not reconcile them: 'each pass retries until the version exists' plus a BRIDGE_ALERT, versus 'a repeat pass writes nothing'. A straightforward implementation that re-emits the alert (or re-attempts and re-logs the outbound write) on every pass while the version is still missing writes new events on an otherwise-unchanged store.
findings.location: Design decisions -> Direction/Missing version; Constraints -> No churn; AC line 'A rebar release naming a version the Jira project lacks...'
scenarios: A rebar ticket carries a release whose Jira version does not yet exist; the bridge runs repeatedly before an admin creates the version — each pass must not append a new alert or re-log an outbound attempt.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Extend the first child's spike to verify the Jira Cloud *ACLI* write surface for fixVersions (observe `jira workitem edit --help`/--from-json schema for an additive fixVersionsToAdd/fixVersionsToRemove operation), not just the REST editmeta/update verb, and name the capability gap + fallback if ACLI offers no additive array operation.
evidence: Plan quote: 'labels change through per-item update verbs ({"update":{"labels":[{"add"|"remove": ...}]}}, Data Center add_field_value / update(remove)), never a whole-list set'; 'fixVersions is an array field and should take the same add/remove update verbs.'
Code: src/rebar/reconciler/adapters/jira/acli_graph.py:143-174 — Cloud add_label uses ACLI payload {"labelsToAdd": [label]} via `jira workitem edit --from-json`, NOT a REST update verb
Code: tests/scripts/bridge/test_bridge_acli_field_coverage.py:372 — 'Use labelsToAdd because ACLI rejects the singular --label flag'
EVIDENCE CLASS: Unverified — no observed ACLI --help / docs for a fixVersions additive operation; the plan itself states the field is 'unverified against the live API'
findings.finding: The plan's 'Jira writes' section names only REST update verbs ({"update":{"labels":[{"add"|"remove"}]}} and DC add_field_value/update(remove)) and asserts fixVersions 'should take the same add/remove update verbs', but the Cloud adapter does not use REST update verbs for labels at all — it drives ACLI (jira workitem edit --from-json with labelsToAdd/labelsToRemove, acli_graph.py:143-188). Whether ACLI exposes an equivalent additive fixVersions operation (e.g. fixVersionsToAdd/fixVersionsToRemove) is unverified and unmentioned, so the Cloud write path is an asserted-but-unverified external capability.
findings.location: Plan section 'List sync follows the tags/labels pattern' -> 'Jira writes' bullet; AC: 'Pinned for both the Jira Cloud and Data Center adapters'
scenarios: Operator sets a release on a rebar ticket bound to a Jira Cloud issue; the bridge needs to write fixVersions additively via ACLI, but ACLI may offer no fixVersionsToAdd/Remove operation
The 'first child' spike checks the REST/editmeta surface but not the ACLI write path, so a Cloud write-path capability gap ships undetected
findings.suggested_fix: In the 'Jira writes' bullet, distinguish the two Cloud/DC write mechanisms: DC via pycontribs add_field_value/update(remove); Cloud via ACLI --from-json. State that the spike must confirm ACLI supports additive fixVersions operations before committing the outbound Cloud work, and record the probe result as Verified/Contradicted.
